title: Repair stale built-in workspace Skill bindings safely
goal: Prevent legacy on-device workspace Skills from remaining unavailable or producing malformed-skill errors solely because their canonical module binding metadata predates the current runtime.
context: FileSkillStore.ensureDefaultSkill only writes canonical workspace Skill files when they do not exist. Existing workspace.create-file, workspace.search, or workspace.read-file files can therefore retain missing host-owned moduleID/chatInputAdapter metadata after an app upgrade. Repair only a parsed canonical Skill with the exact expected ID and input/output schema identifiers; never overwrite custom Skill content or accept mismatched bindings.
forbidden_changes: Do not overwrite arbitrary or malformed custom Skill files.
Do not repair or grant a built-in binding when the Skill ID or schema identifiers do not exactly match the canonical contract.
Do not weaken Agent scope, policy, approval, schema validation, workspace path/protected-file checks, secret detection, size limits, read-back verification, or cancellation.
Do not infer or instantiate arbitrary executor names or module IDs from untrusted Skill metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Existing canonical workspace Skill files missing only host-owned binding metadata are migrated idempotently.
Existing custom, malformed, schema-mismatched, or conflicting-binding Skill files are not overwritten or silently granted a built-in executor.
Regression tests cover migration for each canonical workspace Skill, idempotency, and refusal to rewrite a conflicting or schema-mismatched Skill.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
recovery: Revert the scoped migration if existing user-authored Skill content changes unexpectedly; preserve fail-closed behavior for mismatched bindings.
